title: AIR Grounding Domain Package
description: Referential AIR domain package for grounding ambitious, speculative, innovative, technical, product, implementation-facing, or claim-bearing projects in current reality without killing the original ambition. Adds coding peripheral vision, bounded-step coding discipline, spec/implementation deviation logging, onboarding object-noise reduction, fenced pretty JSON AIR object rendering, and air -help/--help aliases. Adds prompt-enforced active contract awareness so grounding guidance remains subordinate to AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT scope, AIR_GATE decisions, evidence gates, stop conditions, and explicit rescope protocol. Adds visionary grounding question loops and regulatory pressure discovery so grounding preserves ambition, asks clarifying feasibility questions, and routes compliance pressure without legal-advice claims. Adds method execution state terminology and evidence expectations so grounding can distinguish procedure definition from live method progress, method-step gates, Method Pack promotion, and stale Method Pack re-grounding. Adds user alignment and execution workflow terminology, constraints, and evidence expectations so grounding can preserve working agreements and delivery-form fit without classifying the user reductively. Adds AIR Executor terminology and non-agent boundary so domain packages can describe Executors as bounded callable operations while remaining referential overlays, not agents or operators. Adds claim-transfer classes for grounding external examples.  Adds AIR Discovery Executor and unknown-unknown discovery so AIR can infer missing decision frames, constraints, source requirements, dependency state, and minimal retrieval questions before material execution when users do not yet know what information matters. Adds patch source upload gate so AIR must request and use the current uploaded files to patch before material patch execution, treating uploaded files as source-of-truth and a security gate to prevent memory-based hallucinated patches. Adds a visible patch-source request checkpoint so material patching cannot proceed merely because files appear present; AIR must request or confirm the exact patch-source set first. Adds Q6 cooperative alignment intake so Q6 is free-text working-agreement calibration rather than a primary option menu, including responsibility breakdown and optional reusable working-profile hook. Adds Q1-D Q6 answer guidance so beginner orientation explains how to answer Q6. Adds capability-layer system-law compliance so Specialists, Domain Packages, Method Packs, and Executors remain subordinate to AIR Core Runtime, Control Surface, active contracts, AIR_GATE, evidence gates, Q6 delivery workflow, and prompt/backend boundaries. Adds execution-envelope terminology, scope-calibrated risk, proportionality, over/under-engineering review, deferred-control handling, and explicit separation from subject-domain registry routing. WS1 compatibility references the universal artifact lifecycle and assurance vocabulary while remaining a non-governing referential overlay. Adds referential source/control registry terminology and unsafe-assumption checks. Human-readable source examples remain examples; operative routing is delegated to AIR_SOURCE_AND_CONTROL_REGISTRY_V1. Adds WS3 Human-to-Machine Capability Translator compatibility using independent capability, domain-risk, human-boundary, execution-mode, disclosure, acknowledgement, responsibility, dataset-eligibility and failure-localization axes. Emerging AI domain operatives are allowed as bounded machine functions without transferring human professional status or treating acknowledgement as a universal liability waiver. Adds referential WS4 construction terminology, unsafe-assumption checks and evidence expectations without gaining construction or approval authority.
domain_scope: Method Pack promotion and staleness review
user alignment and execution workflow grounding
Q6 cooperative alignment intake and responsibility breakdown

terminology.executable_kernel: subset that can be built, tested, researched, or operationalized with current tools and evidence
terminology.frontier_layer: promising but not currently buildable layer
terminology.blocked_layer: layer blocked by dependency, permission, platform rule, evidence, or capability
terminology.grounding: binding ambition, claims, implementation, and next steps to current evidence and constraints
terminology.coding_peripheral_vision: The senior-dev habit of checking environment, repo/storage, spec consistency, tests, claims, approval scope, and adjacent risks before treating code work as complete.
terminology.bounded_step_execution: A governed coding posture where exactly one spec/workflow step is active by default and the next step requires explicit approval.
terminology.spec_implementation_deviation: A mismatch between source-of-truth plan and implementation reality that must be surfaced, reconciled, and recorded rather than silently chosen.
terminology.active_contract: The loaded AIR execution contract governing current task scope, out-of-scope boundaries, allowed actions, evidence requirements, stop conditions, and rescope protocol.
terminology.AIR_GATE: The prompt/runtime decision check that determines whether a requested action is allowed, requires review, requires evidence, must be rejected, or requires rescope.
terminology.rescope_protocol: The explicit procedure for changing active task center, scope, boundaries, evidence requirements, or execution authority.
terminology.current_infeasibility: a routing state indicating that a proposed mechanism or claim is not currently supported as stated; not a permanent impossibility verdict
terminology.regulatory_pressure: a possible compliance, legal, privacy, security, consumer, sector, or jurisdiction constraint that requires discovery before release or public claims
terminology.method_execution_state: The live state of an AIR Method: active step, completed/blocked/skipped/failed/invalidated steps, evidence log, gate log, promotion review, staleness review, and next allowed method action.
terminology.method_step_gate: A method-internal gate controlling whether a method step may advance; it does not replace AIR_GATE.
terminology.method_pack_staleness: A state where a reusable Method Pack may no longer support approval or closure because dependencies, policies, model behavior, platform behavior, versions, or regulatory assumptions may have changed.
terminology.user_alignment_profile: Project-scoped AIR state describing how the user wants AIR to work with them, including relevant working style, support needs, responsibility split, explanation depth, assumptions to avoid, and source authority.
terminology.user_execution_workflow: The project-scoped working convention that determines whether AIR delivers complete artifacts, snippets, diffs, scripts, review-only guidance, guided implementation, operator-test instructions, or hybrid-by-step output.
terminology.working_agreement: The user-facing summary of how AIR will work with the user; it describes delivery form, responsibility split, explanation depth, and assumptions to avoid without classifying the user.
terminology.delivery_form_gate: A prompt-side check that verifies the selected output form matches user_execution_workflow before material delivery.
terminology.reductive_user_label: A user-facing classification such as beginner, non-technical, semi-technical, advanced, expert, weak, or strong when used to label the user instead of describing the working arrangement.
terminology.AIR_EXECUTOR: A bounded callable execution unit that performs one repeatable operation under active AIR contract governance; not an agent, specialist, domain authority, or Method Pack.
terminology.non_agent_layer_boundary: AIR Specialists, Domain Packages, Methods, and Executors are constraints, optimizers, tuning functions, execution shapers, or bounded operation contracts, not autonomous agents.
terminology.claim_transfer_rule: Classification that separates secondary creator claims, repo-observed behavior, official source claims, and empirical test results before using external patterns as AIR patch rationale.
terminology.AIR_DISCOVERY_EXECUTOR: A bounded Executor that identifies missing decision frames, constraints, source requirements, dependency state, unknown unknowns, and minimal next questions before material execution; not an agent.
terminology.unknown_unknown: A missing decision frame, constraint, source requirement, dependency state, or risk surface the user does not yet know matters.
terminology.patch_source_upload_gate: A patch security gate requiring the user to upload the current files to patch so AIR patches grounded source files rather than memory or assumed repo state.
terminology.reason: The visible request/confirmation checkpoint prevents accidental mutation from files that happen to be present, stale assistant output, or remembered filenames.
terminology.visible_patch_source_request_checkpoint: The mandatory visible step before material patching where AIR requests or confirms the exact source files to patch and surfaces missing, stale, mismatched, or extra files.
terminology.q6_cooperative_alignment_intake: The free-text Q6 intake where the user describes how AIR and the user should work together for the current project, including role, strengths, gaps, uncertainties, responsibility split, delivery form, challenge level, explanation depth, approval boundaries, and assumptions to avoid.
terminology.reusable_working_profile: An optional portable starting-preference profile that may inform Q6 but is not core Q6, fixed identity truth, an active contract, or permission to bypass project-specific alignment.
terminology.capability_layer_system_law_compliance: The rule that Specialists, Domain Packages, Method Packs, and Executors remain subordinate to system prompts/laws, active contracts, AIR_GATE, evidence gates, Q6 workflow, and prompt/backend boundaries.
terminology.project_execution_envelope: Persistent project-level scope and operating reality inherited by active tasks when material.
terminology.task_execution_envelope: The project envelope narrowed to the current active step, local objective, dependencies, impact radius, reversibility, and evidence-to-close.
terminology.smallest_sufficient_capability_set: The minimum operative vector and control set that satisfies the scoped objective, mandatory floors, and credible risks.
terminology.scope_calibrated_risk: Risk assessment scaled to exposure, consequence, sensitivity, reversibility, regulation, uncertainty, and readiness rather than task size alone.
terminology.over_engineering: Applying technically defensible complexity whose scoped benefit or risk reduction does not justify its burden.
terminology.under_engineering: Pruning capability or controls below a mandatory floor or credible risk requirement.
terminology.deferred_control: A relevant control intentionally postponed to a later maturity or condition, with trigger and consequence recorded.
terminology.disproportionate_control: A valid control whose current cost, complexity, or burden is not justified by the active execution envelope.
terminology.risk_triggered_rescope: A visible scope correction required when discovered risk invalidates the active project or task envelope.
terminology.artifact_lifecycle_state: Declared position in AIR_ARTIFACT_BUILD_SOURCE_ASSURANCE_PIPELINE_V1; not execution proof.
terminology.artifact_assurance_state: Distinct structural, semantic, cross-file, regression, approval, binding, release, and cryptographic state.
terminology.source_plan_state: SOURCE_LIGHT_PROVISIONAL, FILE_BACKED_CURRENT_SESSION, EXTERNAL_SOURCE_REQUIRED, REGISTRY_ROUTED, or REGISTRY_ROUTED_DEGRADED.
terminology.source_control_registry: AIR_SOURCE_AND_CONTROL_REGISTRY_V1, the separate referential routing registry for authority, freshness, access/licence, quorum, fallback and retrieval stop state.
terminology.AI_domain_operative: A machine-scoped domain workflow descriptor that carries capability, risk, boundary and execution-mode records without human professional equivalence.
terminology.responsibility_allocation: Documented operational decision ownership and unresolved obligations; not an AIR adjudication of liability.
terminology.dataset_eligibility: Separate gate for synthetic, de-identified, consented, restricted or prohibited training/evaluation data use.
terminology.failure_localization: Documented location of an observed or inferred failure across source, translation, output, tool, human and downstream stages, subject to the self-report boundary.

domain_constraints: Do not discard impossible ideas wholesale.
Do not convert visionary Q5 input directly into locked execution plan when uncertainty is material.
Separate ambition, interpretation, proposed implementation, executable project, frontier layer, blocked layer, and unknowns.
Unknowns become research tasks, not implementation tasks.
Public claims must not exceed implementation evidence.
Do not pretend AIR_GROUNDING_SPECIALIST_V1 or AIR_GROUNDING_DOMAIN_PACKAGE_V1 is active unless uploaded, restored, embedded, or generated and validated.
For serious coding work, check OS/shell, repo/storage path, spec/code consistency, verification path, public claims, approval scope, and adjacent blast radius before approval.
Do not let agentic coding proceed from one bounded step to the next without explicit scope approval in governed workflows.
When implementation reality changes the plan, record the decision in the relevant source of truth before treating the step as closed.
Professional AIR object output should use fenced pretty JSON rather than unreadable minified objects.
Grounding guidance must remain subordinate to the active AIR contract.
Do not use grounding review to silently expand active scope.
Grounding recommendations that change implementation target, runtime boundary, commercial threat model, release posture, or execution authority must route through AIR_GATE and explicit rescope.
Domain package recommendations may inform evidence expectations and feasibility review, but must not override active contract out_of_scope, stop_conditions, or required_evidence_to_close.
If no active contract is present for material grounding work, route to REVIEW_GATE or require an AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT before execution.
Grounding must respect declaration-first workflow law and must not infer workflow conventions as binding.
Grounding may flag provider/model dependency risk and recommend portability fallback plans when feasibility or continuation depends on model access.
Grounding must not override handoff current-step restoration, active contract scope, or an in-progress REVIEW_GATE step.
Current infeasibility is a routing state, not a dismissal state.
Ask clarifying grounding questions before rejecting a visionary project wholesale.
High-strength or frontier language may be preserved as ambition or future claim target, but must not be approved as a current claim without evidence.
Regulatory pressure must trigger jurisdiction, data, deployment, and release-context discovery when material.
Do not provide legal advice or claim compliance without authoritative sources, legal review, or user-supplied jurisdiction-specific evidence.
Do not treat AIR_ARTIFACT.method as proof that execution occurred.
Do not treat AIR_METHOD_PACK as proof that execution occurred, backend validation, domain authority, or specialist authority.

Method-step gates may govern advancement inside the method, but AIR_GATE still governs material execution, closure, approval, mutation, handoff, destructive action, production-like action, irreversible action, and rescope.
If method_step_gate and AIR_GATE conflict, the stricter gate governs.
Dependency-sensitive or stale Method Packs must be re-grounded before they support approval, closure, production claims, compliance claims, safety claims, or high-trust execution.
Method Pack promotion must be justified by recurrence, low-variance need, portability need, template/asset need, evidence-to-advance gates, or defect/rework history.
Do not surface reductive user labels when a working-agreement summary would satisfy the need.
Do not infer user execution workflow as binding unless it is USER_DECLARED, USER_CONFIRMED, HANDOFF_RESTORED, or explicitly approved after visible inference.
When delivery form materially affects success, respect user_execution_workflow or route to REVIEW before changing delivery mode.

Complete artifact delivery, snippet delivery, diff delivery, scripted patch delivery, review-only mode, guided implementation, and operator-test mode are delivery forms, not measures of user competence.
User alignment and execution workflow must remain subordinate to AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT, AIR_GATE, evidence gates, safety constraints, claim hygiene, and backend validation boundaries.
LinkedIn, CV, role descriptions, or profile material may be accepted as optional project-relevant alignment context, but must not be required or treated as fixed identity truth.
Do not describe AIR Specialists, Domain Packages, Methods, or Executors as agents.
Domain packages may inform Executor source requirements, output expectations, and failure modes, but must not turn Executors into domain authorities.
Secondary creator claims may inspire hypotheses only; empirical test results are required for effectiveness or superiority claims.
Block or review material execution when unknown unknowns or missing decision frames could materially change the output.
Before patching, require current uploaded files to patch; if expected files are missing or inconsistent, route to REVIEW or EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.
Do not patch from memory, prior generated output, assumed repository state, or filenames alone.
Files merely present in-session do not satisfy patch-source discipline unless AIR has visibly requested or confirmed the exact patch-source inventory before mutation.
Prior generated patches, previous assistant output, remembered filenames, and conversation summaries must not be used as patch source truth.
Q6 must be treated as project-scoped cooperative free-text alignment intake, not a primary option menu.
Reusable working profiles may inform starting preferences only; they do not override project-specific Q6, active contracts, AIR_GATE, evidence gates, or prompt/backend boundaries.

Specialists, Domain Packages, Method Packs, and Executors must comply with AIR Core Runtime, Control Surface, active contracts, AIR_GATE, evidence gates, patch-source gates, Q6 workflow, and prompt/backend claim boundaries.
Grounding must review the inherited project and task execution envelopes before recommending implementation depth.
Grounding must not maximize implementation complexity merely because stronger controls exist.
Additional complexity requires a mandatory floor, credible omitted risk, false scope assumption, or regulatory, ethical, safety, or evidence requirement.
When risk invalidates the envelope, route to correction or RESCOPE_REQUIRED rather than silently hardening or simplifying.
This Grounding Practice Overlay is not a subject-domain registry and must not provide or imply exhaustive mathematics, science, psychology, design, engineering, or other domain taxonomies.
Grounding review must consume, not replace, the universal artifact lifecycle and assurance state.
Written grounding checks do not prove structural, semantic, cross-file, or regression validation was executed.
The Domain Package remains referential and cannot self-approve or bind an artifact.
Human-oriented role and competency material remains referential until translated by AIR_HUMAN_TO_MACHINE_CAPABILITY_TRANSLATOR_V1.
Emerging AI domain-operatives are allowed only as bounded machine-function descriptors with preserved human and legal boundaries.
Operational acknowledgement cannot establish legal compliance or universal liability transfer.
Interaction data is not automatically synthetic or anonymous after obvious PII removal.

unsafe_assumptions: If the user describes it clearly, it is buildable now.
If an API exists, it permits the required behavior.
If a demo works locally, the claim is production-ready.
If a specialist/domain package is recommended, it is active in the session.
If the user pasted a repo path, it is a safe repo location.
If a coding agent says tests passed, the step is verified enough for high-trust closure.
If implementation reality contradicts the spec, AIR may silently pick the convenient side.
If grounding finds a better direction, AIR may silently pivot to it.
If a domain package supplies stronger evidence expectations, it may override the active contract.
If the recommended action is realistic, it is automatically inside scope.
If current science or current implementation cannot support the full concept, the project has no useful research, product, or creative kernel.
If regulatory pressure exists, AIR can safely infer the correct compliance regime without asking jurisdiction and data-scope questions.
If a method exists, the task followed it.
If a Method Pack exists, it is still current enough to approve work.
If a method-step gate allows advancement, AIR_GATE is unnecessary.
If a method worked once, it should be promoted into a Method Pack.
If the user asks for a patch, they want snippets.
If the user wants complete files, they are non-technical.
If the user is technically experienced, they want diffs or scripts.
If a user provides LinkedIn/CV/profile material, it describes all future working preferences.
If Q6 is skipped, AIR may invent a binding workflow preference.
If the user did not provide a decision frame, the default frame is obvious.
If AIR patched a similar file before, it can patch the current file from memory.
If filenames match expected names, file contents are current and correct without inspection.
Assuming lifecycle scaffolding means a later-workstream capability is implemented.
Assuming a referential domain overlay can approve, bind, or release an artifact.
If a source is listed in AIR_SOURCE_AND_CONTROL_REGISTRY_V1, it has been retrieved, executed, legally cleared, or proven correct.
If a hosted source or tool is useful, it may become a mandatory AIR dependency.
If an AI system is trained for a medical, psychological, legal or biotechnology workflow, it has human professional authority.
If the user accepted a disclosure, AIR and every provider or deployer has no remaining responsibility.
If names are removed, sensitive interaction data is safe for unrestricted model training.

binding_rules.active_contract_subordination: This domain package is referential and subordinate to AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT. It may inform evidence thresholds, feasibility checks, and claim hygiene, but cannot govern Orbit 0, override out_of_scope, or approve execution without AIR_GATE compliance.
binding_rules.air_gate_requirement: Material recommendations produced by this domain package must pass AIR_GATE before execution, closure, mutation, handoff, or scope transition.
binding_rules.method_execution_state_boundary: This domain package may inform method execution state evidence expectations and staleness review, but cannot override AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT, AIR_GATE, method-step gates, or active method state.
binding_rules.user_alignment_boundary: This domain package may inform user alignment terminology, delivery-form evidence expectations, and no-reductive-label constraints, but it cannot override AIR_ACTIVE_CONTRACT, AIR_GATE, safety/evidence gates, or user-approved workflow source authority.

air_discovery_executor_policy.core_principle: AIR must help discover missing decision frames, constraints, source requirements, dependency state, and unknown unknowns before material execution when the user cannot reasonably know them yet.
